summary: Frontend-only regression test of Dashboard resizable-panel id-collision fix and full-width layout fix (per main agent's request). Resize/independence/persistence fixes VERIFIED WORKING. Found one new regression in the App.js full-width fix: layout doesn't update reliably on client-side (SPA) navigation.

ui_bugs.component: App.js <main> full-width conditional (line ~356: `window.location.pathname === '/' ? "w-full" : "container mx-auto p-4 md:p-6"`)
ui_bugs.issue: This check reads window.location.pathname directly during render instead of using the reactive useLocation() hook, and App itself does not subscribe to router location changes. Result: clicking a nav Link (client-side route change, e.g. Dashboard -> /trading) does NOT immediately update the <main> className. Verified deterministically (2/2 trials) that 300ms after clicking nav-trading from Dashboard, main className was still 'w-full' (full-width, no container/padding) instead of switching to 'container mx-auto p-4 md:p-6'. It eventually self-corrects only when App happens to re-render for an unrelated reason (e.g. the 30s account/position poll, or the scanner's 1s countdown state), which is a race condition - sometimes it corrected within ~1s, sometimes it was still wrong after 4s+. A full page reload (direct page.goto) on /trading always shows the correct container layout immediately, so the bug is specific to SPA/client-side navigation.

action_items: In App.js, replace `window.location.pathname === '/'` with the reactive `useLocation()` hook (e.g. `const { pathname } = useLocation(); ... className={pathname === '/' ? 'w-full' : 'container mx-auto p-4 md:p-6'}`) so the layout updates immediately/synchronously on client-side route changes instead of depending on an incidental re-render from polling.
critical_code_review_comments: Dashboard.js / ChartGrid.js: explicit unique id/order props on every ResizablePanelGroup/ResizablePanel confirmed correct and no longer collide - verified via live drag tests (see below). Good fix.
App.js main className logic works correctly on full page load/reload for any route, but is not reactive to React Router client-side navigation - see ui_bugs above.
verified_working: Dashboard (/) renders full-width (main box left=0, right=1920 at 1920x1080 viewport) with no side gutters - confirmed via direct page load.

/trading (and by extension other non-dashboard routes) render with the normal 'container mx-auto p-4 md:p-6' centered/padded layout - confirmed via direct page load (left=192, right=1728, width=1536 at 1920x1080).

Dragging the chart-grid's row1-internal vertical handle (between 10Sec/1Min tiles) resized only row1's two tiles (641/641 -> 491/791px); row2's two tiles (5Min/1Day) remained unchanged at 641/641px - this is the key regression check for the id-collision theory and it PASSED, confirming row1-cols and row2-cols no longer collide.
Dragging the horizontal handle between chart-grid row1/row2 resized the two rows independently and correctly.
Dragging the main sidebar<->chart-area handle and the left-sidebar Stocks<->News handle both worked smoothly without glitching.

After manually resizing panels, waited 13s (covering a data refresh cycle) and re-measured tile pixel dimensions - sizes were byte-for-byte identical before/after, confirming panel sizes do NOT snap back or shift on data refresh.
action_items_note: 10Sec chart tile showing 'No real-time trade ticks yet for this symbol' is expected per main agent's note (MARKET_STREAM_ENABLED=false in this sandbox) - NOT flagged as a bug.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Core resize-independence and persistence bugs from the id-collision theory are CONFIRMED FIXED via live drag tests with screenshots. Dashboard full-width and other-page container layout are also confirmed correct on fresh page loads. The only remaining issue is a minor SPA-navigation layout lag in App.js (see action_items) - low complexity fix (swap to useLocation hook). No backend testing was performed per review scope (frontend only).
rca_of_the_issue: App.js's <main> className is computed inline from `window.location.pathname` at render time. Since App itself has no state tied to the router (only NavBar uses useLocation), clicking a React Router <Link> updates the URL/History but does not by itself force App to re-render, so the stale pathname check lingers until some unrelated state update (polling interval, countdown timer) happens to re-render App. Fix: use `useLocation()` in App so the pathname check is reactive to route changes.
